"Furthermore, I have made it clear that any state request left unfulfilled by these platforms will trigger proceedings to impose financial penalties upon them," Gawkowski also said.

item.title: テラドローンの無人機販売「敵対的」、厳しい対応取る＝ロ外務省
item.description: [モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] - ロシア外務省は２１日、日本企業のテラドローンによるウクライナへのドローン（無人機）販売を「敵対的」な取引と見なすと表明し、厳しい対応を取ると警告した。

ザハロワ報道官は、テラドローンが先週、ウクライナにドローンを納入したと発表したことに対応していると説明。定例記者会見で「テラドローンがウクライナ軍と協力していることは単なる『民間主導の取り組み』に過ぎないとして、これを正当化しようとする日本当局の試みは全く説得力に欠ける」と述べた。

item.title: Anthropic logged net loss of over US$80 billion in first half of 2026
item.description: Anthropic’s net loss widened sharply to US$80.7 billion in the first half of this year, in large part due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into shares of the AI startup, according to a ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Anthropic’s net loss widened sharply to US$80.7 billion in the first half of this year, in large part due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into shares of the AI startup, according to a draft prospectus for a planned initial public offering that was reviewed by Reuters. The San Francisco-based company is expected to go public in November and some investors are now weighing a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion following its latest financial disclosures, Reuters reported last week. Its first-half loss, widening from a loss of $13 billion a year earlier, included a $72 billion accounting charge reflecting an increase in the estimated value of bonds that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash costs tied to its operations, the document said. The disclosures underscore the hefty costs of the AI race even as investors give greater scrutiny to whether the vast sums being poured into chips and data centers will generate sufficient returns. Anthropic has committed to spending at least $518 billion over a decade on cloud services, computing and infrastructure. The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half, up from $2.3 billion a year earlier, the S-1 document showed. Anthropic did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Financing costs At an investor meeting on October 14, Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. While the figures eased some concerns about the enormous costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate. Revenue had more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6 billion in the second quarter. A cooler reception for Anthropic’s IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale’s success, ahead of rival OpenAI’s potential listing next year. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic posted a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, with most of that stemming from a similar accounting charge. As Anthropic’s valuation climbed, the estimated fair value of those notes tripled year over year. Excluding the charge, Anthropic posted an operating loss of about $8.1 billion on $4.6 billion of revenue in 2025. The company has benefited from the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps. Reporting by Echo Wang, Aditya Soni, Jaspreet Singh and Rajveer Singh Pardesi in Bengaluru; Editing by Sahal Muhammed, Miyoung Kim and Thomas Derpinghaus, Reuters

item.title: Münchener Rück verkleinert Vorstand auf zehn Mitglieder
item.description: Der Vorstand der Münchener Rück schrumpft zum 1. November von elf auf zehn Mitglieder. Die für das Europa- und Lateinamerika-Geschäft in der Schaden-Rückversicherung verantwortliche Clarisse Kopff (53) werde das Unternehmen Ende Oktober nach vier Jahren verlassen, teilte der Rückversicherungskonzern am Mittwoch mit. Ihr Vertrag lief noch bis 2030. Kopffs Position werde "dauerhaft nicht nachbesetzt", ihre Aufgaben übernehme Rückversicherungs-Vorstand Thomas Blunck zusätzlich. Die Münchener Rück hatte die Französin 2022 von der Allianz geholt, wo sie den Kreditversicherer Euler Hermes leitete, der inzwischen unter der Marke Allianz Trade auftritt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Vorstand der Münchener Rück (MUVGn.DE) schrumpft zum 1. November von elf auf zehn Mitglieder. Die für das Europa- und Lateinamerika-Geschäft in der Schaden-Rückversicherung verantwortliche Clarisse Kopff (53) werde das Unternehmen Ende Oktober nach vier Jahren verlassen, teilte der Rückversicherungskonzern am Mittwoch mit. Ihr Vertrag lief noch bis 2030. Kopffs Position werde "dauerhaft nicht nachbesetzt", ihre Aufgaben übernehme Rückversicherungs-Vorstand Thomas Blunck zusätzlich. Die Münchener Rück hatte die Französin 2022 von der Allianz (ALVG.DE) geholt, wo sie den Kreditversicherer Euler Hermes leitete, der inzwischen unter der Marke Allianz Trade auftritt.

item.title: Heineken ordered to pay €111 million in damages, interest to Greek rival
item.description: Dutch beer company Heineken on Wednesday said a Dutch court had awarded Macedonian Thrace Brewery €111 million ($125 million) in damages and interest in a case it brought against Heineken's Greek subsidiary Athenian Brewery.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dutch beer company Heineken (HEIN.AS) on Wednesday said a Dutch court had awarded Macedonian Thrace Brewery €111 million ($125 million) in damages and interest in a case it brought against Heineken's Greek subsidiary Athenian Brewery. Heineken said it disagreed with the reasoning of the court and would appeal the decision, which related to conduct by Athenian Brewery in the Greek beer market between 1998 and 2014. In 2015, the Greek competition watchdog had already fined Athenian Brewery €31.5 million for abuse of its dominant position in the production and distribution of beer. In a follow-up case, the Dutch court now awarded MTB €43 million in damages and €68 million in accrued interest. Heineken said that the damages claim made by MTB had not been realistic, and said the court had made assumptions about MTB's sales, pricing and profitability in a hypothetical scenario. "Those assumptions should be carefully tested against the available economic evidence and market developments during the relevant period," the brewer said. "We do not believe the damages awarded adequately reflect those considerations." ($1 = 0.8910 euros)

item.title: How cheap Chinese antibiotics threaten Europe's last major penicillin plant
item.description: Tucked away in the green foothills of the Austrian Alps, the last fully integrated European penicillin plant faces an uncertain future in the shadow of rising Chinese industrial power.
item.dc:creator: Marleen Kaesebier, Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: Tucked away in the green foothills of the Austrian Alps, the last fully integrated European penicillin plant faces an uncertain future in the shadow of rising Chinese industrial power. The reason: China is churning out the same antibiotics and ingredients as the Sandoz factory in Kundl, Austria, at much lower cost for the European market. The falling prices are a boon for cost-conscious European governments' public healthcare programs but an existential threat to the Kundl site - the only one making penicillin from start to finish in Europe, including key active ingredients. After a number of peers announced they were closing or moving production to China, the plant has become a focal point for a widening debate about the West's self-sufficiency. And, just three years after a €200-million ($225-million) expansion that included €50 million of public funds, Sandoz has asked the European Commission to open an anti-dumping investigation that could result in tariff measures against Beijing. If the plant went out of business, Europe "would be fully dependent" on China, Kundl site manager Stephanie Jedner told Reuters in offices looking out over the plant's gleaming storage tanks, ringed by the Tyrolean Alps. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin a century ago in London, and it remains the main antibiotic class for life-threatening infections. Today, the manufacturing of ingredients for some 1.5 billion daily doses Europe administers each year is dominated by China. China's share of EU imports of penicillins and their derivatives in mostly bulk active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) form has nearly doubled from 44% in 2019 to 86% last year, Eurostat data show, coinciding with Beijing's "Made in China" 10-year plan to move up the global manufacturing value chain. Meanwhile, Europe's exports of the same are today barely a fifth of their early 2000s peak. It's one example of how China has graduated from textiles and assembly plants to advanced manufacturing and traditionally European industries from pharmaceuticals to machine tools. With the EU goods trade deficit with China ballooning to around €1 billion per day in 2025, double the level of 2020, [USN:L6N46017V TEXT:"policymakers are scrambling"] for new measures to protect companies and jobs. Sandoz, in written evidence to British lawmakers earlier this year, said Kundl's capacity to supply Europe was "not commercially sustainable" unless governments paid more for penicillin. It argued that Beijing's control of the penicillin supply chain creates an "inherent strategic risk" akin to China's stranglehold on critical minerals. "Antibiotic supply could feasibly become a tool of economic coercion or hybrid warfare, particularly during periods of diplomatic tension," Sandoz wrote in the submission to lawmakers, asking for more support. MEDICINE AS LEVERAGE IN TRADE WARS China spent years establishing itself as a reliable supplier of essential medicines and is increasingly a player in cutting-edge pharmaceuticals. Sandoz says up to 90% of global antibiotic active ingredients are now produced outside Europe, mainly in China, or in India with Chinese chemicals. "This is something that you should worry about," because China's market power gives it leverage to defend strategic interests, said Tim Rühlig, a China analyst at EU foreign policy think tank, the European Union Institute for Security Studies. China could face reputational damage if it used such leverage. Unlike its near monopoly over rare-earth refining, Chinese policy does not frame power in the antibiotic market in national-security terms. Nonetheless, Chinese economist Daokui Li, a former member of the Chinese central bank's monetary policy committee, spooked Western nations during the COVID-19 pandemic when he suggested supplies of APIs should be on the table in trade disputes. One US official in China, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters that Chinese counterparts had suggested in meetings that Beijing could cut off exports of APIs for some medicines as retaliation in a trade conflict. The Chinese foreign ministry said economic and trade differences with the EU could be resolved through dialogue and consultation. "China consistently opposes all forms of trade protectionism," it said in response to Reuters questions. The US State Department did not immediately provide comment. For European policymakers, the withering of such a strategic industry leaves the bloc vulnerable to restrictions on supplies during pandemics or conflicts, said Bostjan Ceh, head of business development at Labena, Slovenia-based pharmaceutical contract research and development firm. "It would seriously compromise Europe's ability to cope with a health crisis," Ceh said. Only after the COVID-19 pandemic – when Europe noticed its dependence on Asian medical supplies – did policymakers begin treating pharmaceutical output as a strategic matter, said Anna Mihaylova, a policy expert at the Medical University of Plovdiv. Alarm bells sounded in 2022, when supplies of amoxicillin, the penicillin type made at Kundl, ran low in Europe during a surge in respiratory infections after the pandemic. A year later, citing repeated shortages, the European Commission approved €28.3 million toward the Kundl expansion, which raised production capacity by 20%. SHIFTING DEPENDENCIES Wearing a white coat and safety goggles, Cecile Stolz, head of Sandoz's manufacturing unit in Kundl, demonstrated in a small vial how green mould is cultivated to make the compound Scottish scientist Fleming in 1928 found destroyed harmful bacteria. Fleming's discovery won him a Nobel prize. For years after, China depended heavily on Europe for production of penicillin and other generic drugs. But Beijing's industrial investment has now reversed the roles, said analyst Rühlig. China's newfound dominance also stems from fewer environmental regulations, drastically lower labour costs and state subsidies, along with investment by Western pharmaceutical companies seeking cost savings. At the Sandoz site, which employs more than 2,000 people, Stolz's team ferments nutrients in metal vats to produce the penicillin. The process is energy intensive, another factor making Europe's producers less competitive: EU electricity prices for energy-intensive industries averaged nearly 50% above China in 2025, International Energy Agency statistics show. Europe's high energy costs are acutely felt at the Kundl plant, which uses as much energy as the nearby city of Innsbruck, home to over 130,000 people, said its manager Jedner at the site Sandoz shares with former parent Novartis (NOVN.S) and chemicals maker BASF < BASFn.DE >. As energy prices rise, Europe's penicillin prices have been flat or falling, she added. CHEAP ANTIBIOTICS, BUT AT WHAT COST? Sandoz complains it cannot raise prices due to competition and the procurement processes of European countries. The Kundl plant remains vulnerable, the company says, because of European governments' policy of procuring medicine based on the lowest price rather than seeking to maintain diverse supplies. The company argues China is flooding the market with cheap APIs. In March, it filed a complaint to the European Commission about China's hold on parts of the antibiotics market. The case centres on proving Chinese amoxicillin APIs are being sold in Europe below production cost, propped up by subsidies. The European Commission is expected to open the anti-dumping probe soon, though the timing remains unclear due to a backlog of complaints, EU trade experts, European officials and China scholars told Reuters. The people told Reuters EU duties were likely to be levied given Europe is hardening its approach to China more broadly. Of 23 ongoing EU anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations, all but three have China as the sole or joint target. The Commission declined to comment. Other outcomes are possible. European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic recently announced a deal with Beijing to lower its exports of hybrid vehicles rather than imposing tariffs, a bid to salvage Europe's automakers. In public statements, Beijing says its subsidy support is in line with WTO rules. It accuses other countries of protectionism hurting global supply chains. As Sandoz struggles with global trade dynamics, its CEO Richard Saynor said that to be sustainable, the life-saving medicines need more pricing power than everyday candy. "I find it upsetting that we sell a pack of antibiotics more cheaply than a packet of Ricola in Switzerland or a Mars Bar in the UK," he told Reuters. "We take a lot of these things for granted – and we take them for granted until they're no longer around."

item.title: Ministerien wollen Pflicht-Elementarschutz für alle Wohnhäuser
item.description: In Deutschland sollen künftig nach den Vorstellungen des Justiz- und des Finanzministeriums alle Wohnhäuser zumindest teilweise gegen die Folgen von Überschwemmungen, Starkregen, Erdrutschen und ähnlichen Naturgefahren versichert werden. Die beiden Ministerien legten am Mittwoch ein Diskussionspapier für einen besseren Schutz gegen Elementarschäden vor, das als Grundlage für Gespräche mit den Bundesländern und den Versichererverbänden dienen soll. Danach sollen neue Wohngebäudeversicherungen künftig standardmäßig einen Elementarschutz mit maximal 20.000 Euro Selbstbehalt enthalten. Bei bestehenden Policen soll der Elementarschutz nach einem Jahr automatisch einbezogen werden, wenn der Versicherungsnehmer nicht widerspricht.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In Deutschland sollen künftig nach den Vorstellungen des Justiz- und des Finanzministeriums alle Wohnhäuser zumindest teilweise gegen die Folgen von Überschwemmungen, Starkregen, Erdrutschen und ähnlichen Naturgefahren versichert werden. Die beiden Ministerien legten am Mittwoch ein Diskussionspapier für einen besseren Schutz gegen Elementarschäden vor, das als Grundlage für Gespräche mit den Bundesländern und den Versichererverbänden dienen soll. Danach sollen neue Wohngebäudeversicherungen künftig standardmäßig einen Elementarschutz mit maximal 20.000 Euro Selbstbehalt enthalten. Bei bestehenden Policen soll der Elementarschutz nach einem Jahr automatisch einbezogen werden, wenn der Versicherungsnehmer nicht widerspricht. Ganz ohne einen Elementar-Versicherungsschutz sollen Haus- und Wohnungseigentümer aber nach dem Willen der SPD-geführten Ministerien in keinem Fall bleiben. Geprüft werden soll allenfalls, ob sie alternativ eine billigere Mindestversicherung abschließen können, bei der sie im Ernstfall aber auf den ersten 100.000 Euro Schaden sitzenbleiben. Das könnte vor allem für Eigentümer attraktiv sein, deren Häuser in hochwassergefährdeten Gebieten liegen und deren Versicherungsprämien deshalb besonders hoch ausfielen. Immerhin 0,4 Prozent aller Wohnhäuser stehen an Orten, wo einmal in zehn Jahren Hochwasser zu erwarten ist. In diesem Fall müssten sie aber akzeptieren, dass ihnen der Staat nicht finanziell unter die Arme greift. Zwar sind 98 Prozent aller Wohngebäude in Deutschland gegen Feuer, Sturm oder Hagel versichert, aber nur 59 Prozent auch gegen Ereignisse wie Überschwemmungen oder Erdrutsche, die im Klimawandel häufiger auftreten dürften als bisher. Im Schnitt verursachen sie in Deutschland nach Angaben des Versicherer-Verbandes GDV Schäden von rund zwei Milliarden Euro pro Jahr. Bei solchen Katastrophen springt meist der Staat mit Steuergeld ein, um teilweise existenzbedrohende Schäden abzumildern. Das zu ändern, hatte sich die schwarze-rote Bundesregierung bereits im Koalitionsvertrag auf die Fahnen geschrieben. Wie das geschehen soll, ist aber umstritten. Nach 25 Jahren Diskussion liege nun dafür ein Vorschlag auf dem Tisch, erklärte Justiz- und Verbraucherschutzministerin Stefanie Hubig. "Unser Vorschlag bietet die Chance, beim besseren Versicherungsschutz vor Flut und Starkregen endlich voranzukommen." Es gelte aber, viele unterschiedliche Interessen unter einen Hut zu bringen. Zudem müsse der Schutz bezahlbar bleiben - für Eigentümer und für Mieter. Diskutiert werden solle unter anderem, ob Eigentümer die Kosten für den erweiterten Schutz über die Nebenkosten auf die Mieter abwälzen dürfen oder nicht. Die Länder und Verbände haben bis zum 2. Dezember Zeit, sich zu den Vorschlägen zu äußern. Erst danach soll ein Gesetzentwurf ausgearbeitet werden. Der Gesamtverband der Deutschen Versicherungswirtschaft (GDV) sieht eine Versicherungspflicht bisher kritisch und pocht flankierend auf mehr Prävention. Bauverbote etwa in Überschwemmungsgebieten sind in dem Vorschlag der Ministerien ebenso angesprochen wie die staatliche Förderung von Schutzmaßnahmen für gefährdete Häuser.

item.title: Water rationing, rubbish pile-up raise disease fears in Yemen's besieged Taiz
item.description: Fighting between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-allied Houthi group since September has cut key supply routes, worsening shortages of water, food and fuel in and around the city.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Families have started rationing water in and around [USN:L8N46125M TEXT:"Yemen's Taiz city"], where renewed fighting has disrupted fuel supplies and access to water systems serving 3 million people, aid groups and UN agencies said. Meanwhile, mounting piles of rubbish along major roads are raising fears of disease outbreaks in the city, Yemen's third-largest. Fighting between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-allied Houthi group since September has cut key supply routes, including the Taiz-Aden corridor, worsening [USN:L6N4620L1 TEXT:"shortages of water, food and fuel"] in and around the city. The lack of fuel is hampering the operation of water pumps and hospitals, while disruption to waste collection has left rubbish piled along roads of the city, a stronghold of anti-Houthi forces which is now under siege by the armed movement. The Taiz governorate hosts nearly half of the 250,000 people displaced by the latest escalation, aid groups said. "The state of the rubbish in the city is very wretched, and the build-up is terrible, like nothing before,” Taiz resident Abdelbari al-Qadi told Reuters. Sanitation worker Ali Ahmed said authorities could no longer go to the main dumping site because of clashes, and they were forced to burn it in the streets. 'EXTREMELY DANGEROUS SITUATION' FOR CHILDREN, SAYS RELIEF OFFICIAL Families are rationing drinking water as diesel shortages hobble pumping stations and sanitation systems, said Akhil Iyer, UNICEF's representative in Yemen. "I get the water with difficulty. We wait in queues from the morning until our turn comes,” Alaa Khalil told Reuters while people queued to fill jerry cans in Taiz, where most residents depend on trucked water. Access to the Al-Dhubab aquifer, a major source of trucked water for Taiz, has been restricted, while fuel disruptions have affected pumps, creating a severe water crisis, said Wathiq Aghbari, director general of the Local Water and Sanitation Authority in the governorate. Water production in Taiz has fallen by about 50%, according to Save the Children. “We find children in an extremely dangerous situation where they are not able to have their basic needs satisfied. They are not able to access sufficient food and water and healthcare,” said Rishana Haniffa, Save the Children's country director for Yemen. Aid groups are exploring other sources, including a shallow aquifer west of the city. The cost of a water truck has tripled from about 23,000 Yemeni rials ($14.80) before the latest escalation to about 70,000 rials ($45), according to UNICEF. CARE International says cash assistance is buying less food and water as prices rise. “We feel the situation is really getting out of hand unless we able to negotiate access to have water tankers come in to the city,” said Iman Abdullahi, CARE Yemen country director. RUBBISH BUILD-UP 'WILL CAUSE DISEASES', SAYS HEALTH OFFICIAL "The build-up of rubbish is very harmful and will cause diseases, whether respiratory or otherwise," said Abdulrahman al-Sabri, director of Taiz Governorate's Health Office, adding that dengue fever and cholera cases were spreading. Cholera cases have tripled since early September from 221 to 683 this month, while hospitals face medicine shortages and 12 facilities have fuel supplies sufficient for only about four days, the World Health Organization said. A doctor who asked not to be named for security reasons said some families could not reach healthcare facilities because of fighting around the city. The Danish Refugee Council said the impact of deteriorating water and sanitation conditions could spread beyond Taiz city. It pointed to overstretched resources in crowded displacement sites across the governorates of Taiz, Lahj, Abyan and Aden. The spread of disease could also worsen hunger in Taiz governorate, UNICEF said. It has identified 52,000 acutely malnourished children in Taiz so far this year. Road closures have halted UNICEF's deliveries of a therapeutic food for severely malnourished children in Taiz.

item.title: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord, Ankara says
item.description: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said. In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the "Badr Memorandum of Understanding" in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships. "The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. "By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defense industrial capacities, and enable the fulfillment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added. Turkey, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war. In August, it signed a [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"mutual defence pact"] with nuclear-armed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"attack on all"]. Ankara also has [USN:L4N3TQ07F TEXT:"close ties"] with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry. The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives.

item.title: TAUX Le rendement de l'OAT à 10 ans atteint 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002 (actualisé)
item.description: Le rendement de l'obligation souveraine française à 10 ans a atteint mercredi le seuil psychologique de 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002, un nouveau signe de l'inquiétude des investisseurs quant à la capacité de la deuxième économie de la zone euro à réduire son déficit.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Le rendement de l'obligation souveraine française à 10 ans a atteint mercredi le seuil psychologique de 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002, un nouveau signe de l'inquiétude des investisseurs quant à la capacité de la deuxième économie de la zone euro à réduire son déficit. Le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans prend 7 points de base (pdb) pour s'établir à 4,9877% à 12h00 GMT, après avoir brièvement dépassé les 5% plus tôt en séance. Les craintes concernant le budget de la France pour 2027, en plein examen parlementaire, ainsi que la polarisation des débats politiques à la suite des violences en marge des mobilisations du week-end dernier, ont de nouveau mis à rude épreuve le marché obligataire, déjà sous pression en raison de la flambée de l'inflation liée à la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Bien que les tensions sur le marché obligataire soient généralisées, elles sont particulièrement intenses dans les pays les plus endettés, comme la France ou l'Italie ; le rendement des obligations de cette dernière prend plus de six pdb mercredi, pour s'établir à 4,5874%. En Allemagne, dont l'obligation à 10 ans sert de référence pour la zone euro, le rendement du Bund n'avance que de 2 pdb, à 3,4143% Le "spread", c'est-à-dire l'écart de rendement entre les obligations d'État allemandes et françaises, a de nouveau frôlé mercredi les 160 pdb, évoluant à des niveaux qui n'ont plus été observés depuis fin 2011. Il ressort à 157 en début d'après-midi. Le "spread" est un indicateur de la prime de risque exigée par les investisseurs pour détenir des titres de dette français par rapport à ceux de Berlin, considérés comme plus sûrs. "Remettre les finances publiques en ordre passerait notamment par l'adoption d'un budget cet automne qui irait dans le sens d'une réduction du déficit. Mais les finances publiques sont avant tout un enjeu de long terme et le résultat de l'élection présidentielle sera à ce titre déterminant", écrit dans une note Sylvain Bersinger, économiste et fondateur du cabinet Bersingéco. L'approche de l'élection présidentielle de 2027 constitue ainsi un facteur d'incertitude qui exacerbe encore davantage les tensions, d'autant plus que les options les plus extrêmes sont en tête dans les sondages. "On comprend, à la vue des sondages, la frilosité des investisseurs envers la dette française", dit-il. La hausse des rendements obligataires a des répercussions sur l'ensemble de l'économie, rendant les emprunts plus coûteux, y compris le crédit immobilier. "Le seuil des 4% n'a été dépassé que fin juillet, faisant du troisième trimestre, celui de la plus forte hausse des taux d'emprunt d'Etat français en près de 40 ans", souligne Julie Bachet, directrice générale de Vousfinancer, un réseau de 150 agences de courtage en crédit immobilier. "Les taux moyens sur 20 ans sont autour de 3,7%, soit plus d'un point sous l'OAT. Les banques rognent donc sur leurs marges pour continuer à prêter. Cette situation ne peut pas durer indéfiniment et les barèmes vont continuer à augmenter dans les prochaines semaines, plus rapidement que nous ne l'avions prévu", souligne-t-elle.

Oct 21 : Self-driving truck company Einride said on Wednesday it would broaden its partnership with Nvidia by testing the chipmaker's AI reasoning model, Alpamayo, in its self-driving vehicles, aiming to speed up the expansion of autonomous freight services while lowering development costs. Alpamayo is Nvidia's vision language action model, which can interpret driving environments, recommend vehicle actions and explain its reasoning. • The Swedish company said it plans to become the first trucking operator to deploy Alpamayo, adapting the model using data collected from its commercial freight operations • Einride said the technology could help shorten development cycles and make it easier to extend autonomous driving capabilities to new vehicle types and routes, with a live road evaluation planned for the second half of 2027

item.title: GSK is two shots away from clean bill of health
item.description: One of Europe’s most cheaply valued drugmakers, the £75 bln group run by Luke Miels is turning a corner. Fears over expiring patents are easing thanks to a booming oncology unit. A £40 bln sales target looks hard, but Miels may fix that with canny dealmaking and luck in the lab.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Donnellan
item.content:encoded: If GSK (GSK.L) were a patient doctors would be starting to hope that it’s on the mend. Despite being one of the cheapest of the global pharma stocks, new CEO Luke Miels is ploughing money into research and development and doing savvy deals. The big question is can he deliver on his target of over £40 billion in sales by 2031 . Signs of a recovery have appeared slowly. When Miels’ predecessor Emma Walmsley was in charge, she spun out the consumer goods business which makes Sensodyne toothpaste, now called Haleon (HLN.L) . Investors hoped the surgery would unleash a leaner, less indebted business that could focus its efforts on dealmaking and its core areas of vaccines, HIV and general medicines including inhalers and antibiotics. So far, that's yet to translate into a material valuation bump: GSK trades at around 10 times forward earnings, in line with its multiple when Haleon was spun off in 2022 , and below peers like AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , Novartis (NOVN.S) and Roche (ROPC.S) . The main reason is fear of what comes next. Dolutegravir, GSK’s star HIV treatment which accounted for 17% of GSK’s near £33 billion of sales last year, loses patent protection in the US from 2028. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha expect revenue in that division to half by 2031. Vaccines have also lost steam. Anti vaccine sentiment is growing in the US, and analysts expect the division to grow sales by an average of less than 2% over the next five years. However, Miels is plugging these holes partly by bolstering the group’s growing cancer business. Last year, sales in oncology rose by over 40% to nearly £2 billion and they are expected to reach over £5 billion pounds by 2031. And he’s hoping to boost that further through deals and in-house drug development. In June, he splurged [USN:L6N42H0KM TEXT:"$11 billion"] on US lung cancer specialist Nuvalent. The business won regulatory approval for one of its drugs a month after the deal was announced and GSK is expecting to hear about another remedy later this year. This week GSK won regulatory backing for a new rectal cancer drug. Growth in GSK’s oncology business should help offset the decline in HIV as dolutegravir's patents expire. The cancer success isn't the only sign that GSK's plan to boost in-house drug development is paying off. Miels is expecting to start over 20 new late stage drug trials this year. Potential blockbuster drugs include a hepatitis B remedy bepirovirsen which it reckons will generate £2 billion in annual sales. Berenberg analysts estimate the group's likely return on research investment is now over 10%, healthily exceeding the sector's 8% cost of capital. GSK is still some way off hitting Miels' target to reach £40 billion of sales by 2031. But the gap is closing: Analysts polled by Visible Alpha estimate sales of £37 billion that year, up from less than £34 billion a year ago. To hit the magic number, Miels will probably need to do more small deals, as well as keep securing fresh drug approvals. But the danger that he will resort to more large risky takeovers is probably easing. That, along with GSK's broader turnaround, means its valuation should start to catch up with its healthier peers. Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn . GSK will unveil its third quarter earnings on October 28. The US Food and Drug Administration on October 19 approved GSK’s Jemperli, an immunotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: US Democratic congressional nominee Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank
item.description: Brad Lander, an ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani who is running for the US Congress next month, was among 90 individuals detained by Israeli authorities in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, according to Rabbis for Human rights, an Israeli rights group.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brad Lander, an ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani who is running for the US Congress next month, was among 90 individuals detained by Israeli authorities in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, according to Rabbis for Human rights, an Israeli rights group. Lander is a Jewish American and former New York City comptroller and mayoral candidate who has criticized Israel's war in Gaza. He is the Democratic party's nominee for New York's 10th congressional district for the US House of Representatives. There was no immediate comment from Israel Police or the US Embassy in Jerusalem. (This story has been corrected to change the day to Wednesday, from Tuesday, in paragraph 1.)

item.title: Husqvarna looks east as Chinese rivals chip away at robot lawnmower lead
item.description: Husqvarna has moved some production of robotic lawnmowers from Britain to the Czech Republic and is weighing increased manufacturing in Asia, its CEO said on Wednesday, as cheaper rivals chip away at its lead in the market it pioneered three decades ago.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Calero
item.content:encoded: Husqvarna (HUSQb.ST) has moved some production of robotic lawnmowers from Britain to the Czech Republic and is weighing increased manufacturing in Asia, its CEO said on Wednesday, as cheaper rivals chip away at its lead in the market it pioneered three decades ago. Drought across much of Europe left less grass to mow during the third quarter, hurting sales at a time when consumers were already holding back on garden equipment purchases. But the problems go beyond the weather. "We have lost some volume this year," CEO Glen Instone told Reuters, saying Husqvarna had lost more European market share in units sold than in sales value. The Swedish company has held its ground among traditional dealers, but faces much tougher competition in shops and online, sales channels in which it has historically been less active. That is forcing it to reconsider how much it can cut prices without undermining the premium positioning that has long distinguished its products. Instone said Husqvarna would likely have to lower the roughly €1,000 ($1,122) starting price of its Husqvarna-branded robotic mowers, though he ruled out competing with machines costing less than €500. The challenge extends to how and where Husqvarna makes its machines. Instone said the company had moved some robotic mower production from Newton Aycliffe in Britain to Czechia to cut costs. The transfer was completed this autumn and affected around 50 roles in the British plant, a company spokesperson said. Instone said Husqvarna was also considering production in Asia, although longer shipping times and the need to hold more stock could eat into potential savings from such a move. The company said earlier on Wednesday it was moving production of some battery-powered handheld tools from two European factories to Asia, including its own plant in China and external suppliers, with the move to be fully effective in 2028. It did not specify how many jobs would be affected. Just last year, Husqvarna had begun moving production from China to Europe to reduce its exposure to US tariffs. Its Czech subsidiary also initiated an EU investigation into alleged dumping of Chinese robotic mowers last year, although Instone said Husqvarna could compete without additional duties. Despite 935 million Swedish crowns ($94.4 million) of realised savings this year, weak sales and rising costs have continued to erode Husqvarna's earnings. But Instone said further savings could restore profitability in 2027 even without European demand recovery. The company's shares plunged around 10% to a 14-year low in Stockholm after a bigger-than-expected [USN:L8N467068 TEXT:"quarterly loss"]. ($1 = €0.8910) ($1 = 9.9050 Swedish crowns)

item.title: South Korea's Korai Flix to go public in US via $3.5 billion SPAC deal
item.description: South Korean entertainment platform Korai Flix will go public in the U.S. through a $3.5 billion merger with special purpose acquisition company APEX Tech Acquisition , the companies said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean entertainment platform Korai Flix will go public in the U.S. through a $3.5 billion merger with special purpose acquisition company APEX Tech Acquisition (APXBU.O) , the companies said on Wednesday. The deal comes as SPACs, an alternative route to public markets, are [USN:L4N44P1H0 TEXT:"making a comeback"] in the US after years of subdued activity. Korai's platform, launched in 2024, offers AI-generated short dramas and AI companion avatars to roughly 26 million users across 15 countries in Asia. Users can also use tools to create such content in various visual styles. Microdramas, short episodic vertical videos delivered in two-minute episodes for viewing on phones, [USN:L6N44B0T8 TEXT:"have surged in popularity"] worldwide. The format is cheap to produce and can be generated rapidly using artificial intelligence. In the first half of 2026, microdramas on YouTube garnered more than 6.5 billion views, while watch time grew over 50% from a year earlier. Korean entertainment content is also flourishing across the world following the success of K-pop, K-dramas and other Korean cultural exports. Korai will be the latest South Korea-linked entertainment platform to go public in US. Naver-backed Webtoon Entertainment (WBTN.O) , which owns novel distribution platform Wattpad, [USN:L4N3IP1AL TEXT:"debuted in New York in 2024"] through a traditional IPO. A SPAC is a shell company that raises capital through an initial public offering and then uses the funds to merge with or acquire a private company, taking it public without a traditional IPO. The SPAC deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The combined company will be renamed Krflix Group and is expected to list on the New York Stock Exchange.

FAST

Oct 21 : Elon Musk sees "a lot of merit" in combining Tesla and SpaceX, but the decision is not his to make: two special committees he cannot join and a Tesla shareholder vote he calls a high hurdle stand in the way. That tension runs through a deal that many analysts call inevitable. Musk, a self-described 'conflicted party', said the committees are yet to agree on the terms and a merger is not certain, even though Wall Street expects a deal by the end of next year. Shares of SpaceX were up 8.4 per cent, while Tesla gained 1.5 per cent in premarket trading. SpaceX and Tesla are jointly developing the Terafab chip plant, and AI now makes up more than half of SpaceX's revenue, with another $35 billion to $40 billion spending likely in fourth quarter to fund further expansion.

"I think a Tesla-SpaceX merger makes sense. It's very strategic because both companies are rapidly transitioning into artificial intelligence and autonomous systems, and both have huge infrastructure projects underway," said Justus Parmar, CEO of Fortuna Investments and an investor in both companies. "It would also avoid redundancy and the time he spends going back and forth between two entities, and there would be a reduction in public company overhead, legal costs and administrative burdens." Analysts have said that burgeoning capital spending for expensive AI and space infrastructure would weigh on SpaceX's free cash flow, a strain a combined company could ease by sharing services and borrowing jointly with Tesla. They also point to last week's Roadster unveiling, where a Tesla car built with SpaceX rocket thrusters flipped and leapt over a truck, as a teaser for what a combined company could produce. TESLA'S VOTE IS THE HURDLE Control may also be part of Musk's appeal for a merger. Musk holds about 85 per cent of SpaceX's voting power through super-voting shares. But at Tesla he has roughly 20 per cent. Bill Birmingham, head of research at REX Financial, estimates a merger would give the billionaire about 57 per cent of voting rights. Ryan Zurrer, founder of Dialectic, puts it at 58 per cent at an exchange ratio of 0.7 of one SpaceX share, the illustrative level Barclays has floated. No ratio has been negotiated. Zurrer said a ratio near 0.6 would be needed for Musk to keep control if he sold more equity, and that "the biggest hurdle will be the Tesla shareholders vote vs Elon's own incentives". Musk said Tesla side needs a majority of all shares, not just those voted, so every uncast ballot counts against a deal. Analysts have flagged turnout as a risk, citing uncast broker votes at last year's meeting as a potential factor that could affect chances of a deal going through. Governance and regulatory questions would follow. When Tesla bought SolarCity in 2016, a Delaware court cleared it after years of litigation but said it should have formed an independent committee. "A deal where one man runs both sides will draw tough questions on governance," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for APAC at eToro. The business case, not just the process, could also decide it. Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said if Tesla is better off exploring AI synergies with other companies, the deal "could be rejected by investors". Tesla is set to report third-quarter results after markets close. Analysts said they were also watching out for disclosures of merger talks in regulatory filings ahead of the automaker's December 3 annual shareholder meeting.

Source: Reuters

item.title: AT&T raises annual profit forecast on strong demand for bundled plans
item.description: AT&T raised its annual adjusted profit forecast on Wednesday after beating quarterly revenue and profit estimates, betting on its service bundles to drive growth and keep customers from switching to rivals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AT&T (T.N) raised its annual adjusted profit forecast on Wednesday after beating quarterly revenue and profit estimates, betting on its service bundles to drive growth and keep customers from switching to rivals. About 43% of households signing up for AT&T's internet services also opt for its wireless plans, helping the company build stickier customer relationships and reduce disconnects as competition intensifies in the US telecom market. AT&T added 379,000 net monthly bill-paying wireless subscribers during the third quarter, compared with 379,300 additions estimated by FactSet The company also reported a $2.6 billion non-cash impairment charge related to the [USN:L6N45Z18X TEXT:"planned sale"] of its Mexico wireless business for $2 billion It now expects annual adjusted profit per share of about $2.40, compared with its prior forecast of $2.25 to $2.35 US carriers are looking beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions to bundled services and customer loyalty programs to attract and retain subscribers AT&T has been doubling down on fiber expansion, striking a [USN:L4N45L15B TEXT:"multi-year deal"] worth more than $3 billion with Corning last month for fiber and cable supplies It also acquired Lumen's [USN:L6N3RT0UJ TEXT:"fiber business"] in May 2025 for $5.75 billion to expand its broadband footprint and meet rising demand for high-speed connectivity This has helped AT&T secure record broadband additions, with 442,000 new fiber internet users and 327,000 new fixed wireless subscribers added in the third quarter Revenue for the quarter rose 5.3% from a year earlier to $32.3 billion, beating analysts' estimates of $31.69 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG Adjusted profit per share for the quarter came in at 65 cents, above estimates of 60 cents Shares of the company fell 3.8% in volatile premarket trading

item.title: Nasdaq futures lead gains as SpaceX, Super Micro results lift AI stocks
item.description: Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday as quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer revived the AI trade, while Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress investors.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Agarwal, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday as quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer revived the AI trade, while Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress investors. Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm (SPCX.O) rose 7.2% in premarket trading after he said on Tuesday that [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX"] and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea". SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. Tesla shares were up 1.4%. "There is potential for substantial gains in its AI business, as AI infrastructure is capital intensive, and SpaceX has more means than many smaller companies ... if AI stress mounts, SpaceX could swallow up infrastructure business from smaller competitors," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote. Ozkardeskaya said that a merger with Tesla could be a good idea if "the two companies can prove that the synergies create value for both of them", but could be rejected by investors if Tesla was "better off exploring AI synergies with other companies". Other space stocks were also higher, with Rocket Lab (RKLB.O) , Planet Labs (PL.N) and Intuitive Machines (LUNR.O) adding between 2.6% and 3.9%. EchoStar (ECHO.O) , which holds SpaceX shares, rose 4.3%. Super Micro (SMCI.O) jumped 10.9% after the AI server maker [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. Peers HPE (HPE.N) and Dell (DELL.N) rose 4.5% and 5.5% respectively. Investors drew comfort from the reports as concerns over the profitability of the AI buildout triggered a selloff in AI-linked stocks last week, with data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) at the center of the storm. It was up 2.5% before the bell on Wednesday. Most chipmakers also rose, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) up 2.1%, Intel (INTC.O) gaining 2.3% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) adding 1.9%. Semiconductors have had a volatile month so far, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) marking eight consecutive sessions of declines, its longest losing streak in 18 years. Despite a brief reprieve on Monday, the index is trading at two-month lows. The Dow outshone the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq on Tuesday on the back of robust gains in healthcare stocks. On the other hand, Netflix (NFLX.O) dropped over 6.6% after the streaming giant issued [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"a weaker-than-expected forecast"] for its fourth-quarter profit, days after laying off 6% of its workforce. Results from Meta (META.O) and Tesla will be parsed after markets close. At 7:34 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 64 points, or 0.12%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 20.75 points, or 0.27%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 196.75 points, or 0.67%. Before the bell, AT&T (T.N) fell 3.5% despite beating [USN:L4N4670UN TEXT:"third-quarter"] revenue and profit estimates. Elevance Health (ELV.N) rose around 1% after the [USN:L4N4670SF TEXT:"health insurer"] lifted its 2026 profit forecast. Meanwhile, oil prices remained elevated, with Brent crude futures trading near $110 a barrel. Data last week confirmed that price pressures were seeping into the US economy, and had broadened out beyond energy products, supporting the case for another interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. The central bank meets next week.

item.title: プーチン氏、元教師の米国人を解放と表明
item.description: [モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２１日、２０２２年から同国で拘束されていた元教師の米国人スティーブン・ハバード氏（７４）が解放され、サンクトペテルブルクのプルコボ空港にいると表明した。ロシア国営メディアが報じた。これ以上の詳細は明らかにされていない。

ミシガン州出身のハバード氏は、非公開の裁判で雇い兵活動を行ったとして有罪判決を受け、ロシアで７年近くの刑に服していた。

ハバード氏は２２年４月、ウクライナ東部のイジューム市で逮捕された。ロシア検察当局は、同氏が同地でウクライナ軍の検問所の警備にあたっていたと主張していた。

ロシア国営メディアは、ハバード氏が起訴内容について有罪を認めたと報じた。しかし、米国を拠点とする同氏の弁護士マーティン・デ・ルカ氏は以前、ロイターに対し、ハバード氏から「自分に対する罪状は虚偽であり、いかなる戦闘部隊や軍事部隊にも所属していなかった」と伝えられていたことを明らかにしている。

Kimmich's absence is another setback for Bayern, who are also without suspended winger Michael Olise for the group-stage encounter at the Allianz Arena. The German side will nevertheless take confidence from Saturday's 6-1 Bundesliga win over RB Leipzig as they look to build on last week's entertaining 3-3 draw away to Viking in Europe.

Source: Reuters
