item.title: France's Macron vows no repeat of riots as Yellow Vests mobilise
item.description: The Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a major Paris march on Saturday that will present the government with its next big test.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to prevent a repeat of [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"last weekend's"] riots and looting, as the Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a major Paris march on Saturday that will present the government with its next big test. Macron said on Wednesday that those seeking to cause disorder at the next protests would be stopped, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met union leaders in an effort to defuse one of the worst crises France has faced in recent years. A representative of the "Gilets Jaunes" (Yellow Vests) movement, a grassroots group not tied to the unions, presented plans for a march across the heart of Paris, including areas that were ransacked just days ago. Student groups have also called for protests the same day to push demands for greater investment in education. Yellow Vest activists are seeking to revive their campaign, which emerged in 2018, against rising living costs and declining public services. INVESTORS FRET, FRENCH BORROWING COSTS CLIMB Last weekend's demonstrations rapidly degenerated into rampant violence, especially in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], which the overwhelmed police took hours to contain. Highlighting investor concern over the situation, French government borrowing costs have jumped this week, pushing benchmark 10-year bond yields to 5%, [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"their highest level"] since July 2002. Analysts said the move reflected worries that the unrest could complicate government efforts to repair strained public finances at a time of already mounting budget pressures. Macron said he would meet intelligence officials, Lecornu and other ministers on Thursday to obtain a detailed account of the October 17 unrest. "Those who want to cause disorder in city centres next Saturday will be prevented from doing so," Macron told reporters during a visit to Qatar, where he has been seeking energy deals as France grapples with rising fuel costs. "There must be no wavering at the top of the state." MACRON SAYS TRUMP SPREADING MISLEADING INFORMATION Government ministers have promised a vastly reinforced security operation after acknowledging shortcomings in their initial response, with troops expected to be deployed alongside additional police. Macron accused some foreign leaders of spreading misinformation about what had happened. US President Donald Trump in particular [USN:L1N46602Q TEXT:"has blamed"] the turbulence on mass migration and radical Islam, saying it was a warning for Americans. Asked whether he was referring to Trump, Macron said: "Among others", adding that some foreign politicians were looking to make political capital at the expense of France. "We don’t need that. We already have difficulties to deal with," he said. 'LEGITIMATE ANGER' In a letter to unions ahead of Wednesday's meeting, Lecornu said their talks should focus on ensuring "the indispensable freedom to demonstrate", which he said some were trying to curtail by associating it with "unacceptable acts". France's main unions have separately called a nationwide mobilisation for November 5. "There is huge and legitimate anger, and the answer to that situation is not repression. It is a political response. That's what I will tell the prime minister today," Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, told RTL radio. After the meeting, Binet told reporters the government made no new announcements, but did say that youth organisations would be invited for talks. A second consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas hit by the unrest, offering the government some respite as it prepared for fresh demonstrations. The unrest has triggered a political backlash ahead of presidential elections next year, with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls. "The government has lost control of everything," far-right leader Marine Le Pen told Franceinfo radio. The hard-left France Unbowed (LFI), which has denied allegations by ministers of fueling the unrest, criticised plans to deploy troops onto the streets of Paris. "Demonstrators are not enemies within. The French government must not go to war against its own people," LFI's parliamentary group said in a statement. Protests in other European countries, including [USN:L1N4650LE TEXT:"Italy"] and [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"Albania"], have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes. [USN:L8N4661X4 TEXT:"Italy approved"] a raft of security measures on Tuesday, including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration and tougher penalties for rioters in response to the turbulence last weekend.

item.title: Nvidia-Chef Huang sieht großes Robotik-Potenzial in Europa
item.description: Der US-Chipkonzern Nvidia vertraut auf die Wachstumsaussichten europäischer Firmen. "Im zurückliegenden Jahr haben wir nahezu zehn Milliarden Dollar investiert", sagte Konzernchef Jensen Huang am Mittwoch in seiner Rede zum Auftakt der Konferenz GTC in Berlin. "Allein in der letzten Woche haben wir Beteiligungen an 14 Startups verkündet. Insgesamt sind wir inzwischen mehr als 12.000 Partnerschaften eingegangen."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der US-Chipkonzern Nvidia (NVDA.O) vertraut auf die Wachstumsaussichten europäischer Firmen. "Im zurückliegenden Jahr haben wir nahezu zehn Milliarden Dollar investiert", sagte Konzernchef Jensen Huang am Mittwoch in seiner Rede zum Auftakt der Konferenz GTC in Berlin. "Allein in der letzten Woche haben wir Beteiligungen an 14 Startups verkündet. Insgesamt sind wir inzwischen mehr als 12.000 Partnerschaften eingegangen." Der kalifornische Halbleiterhersteller hält unter anderem Anteile an den deutschen Roboterbauern Agile Robots und Neura Robotics, dem KI-Entwickler Black Forest Labs sowie dem Satelliten-Hersteller Reflex Aerospace. Vor allem im Bereich humanoider Robotik habe Europa großes Potenzial, betonte Huang. "Keine Region hat sich so sehr der Herstellung von Mechatronik, Elektronik und mechanischen Systemen auf höchstem Niveau verschrieben wie Europa." Die dadurch gewonnenen Fertigkeiten und Daten bildeten eine hervorragende Grundlage für sogenannte Physische KI. Zur Demonstration holte der Nvidia-Chef mehrere "Microducks" auf die Bühne. Diese KI-gesteuerten zweibeinigen Roboter eines französischen Startups reagieren auf gesprochene Anweisungen. Sie setzen sich hin, schlagen Rad oder machen ein Nickerchen. VORKONFIGURIERTE SYSTEME FÜR ROBOTER UND ROBOTAXIS Um die Verbreitung humanoider Roboter zu beschleunigen, will Nvidia ein vorkonfiguriertes System anbieten. Entwickler müssten sich dann nicht erst mit der Abstimmung von Mechanik, Sensoren und Software herumschlagen, bevor sie die Maschinen für bestimmte Aufgaben trainieren, betonte Huang. Hierfür hat sein Unternehmen in Zusammenarbeit mit dem deutschen Startup Agile den "[USN:L6N4650VU TEXT:"Agile One SN"]" entwickelt. Der etwa 1,4 Meter große und 43 Kilogramm schwere zweibeinige Roboter ist vor allem für Forschungslabore gedacht. Huang stellte bei seiner Präsentation darüber hinaus "Hyperion" vor. Dabei handelt es sich um ein vorkonfiguriertes System aus Hard- und Software für autonome Fahrzeuge. Mithilfe dieser Technologie würden die Robotaxis unterschiedlicher Fahrdienst-Vermittler zu einer riesigen virtuellen Flotte vereinigt. Künftig würden auch Volkswagen, Volvo (VOLCARb.ST) und Mercedes (MBGn.DE) auf "Hyperion" setzen. Huangs Auftritt am Mittwoch wurde kurz durch Zwischenrufe unterbrochen. In der Übertragung der Veranstaltung waren ihre Forderungen nicht zu verstehen. Der Nvidia-Chef sicherte den Störern zu, er werde später mit ihnen sprechen. Sie wurden anschließend aus dem Saal geführt.

item.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安 景気対策への期待後退
item.description:
Summer Zhen
[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安　景気対策への期待後退 19:08 配信

Summer Zhen

[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手 のＣＡＴＬ株は香港・本土市場ともに１０％超急落。競争激化と中国の自動車販売の伸び鈍化を受け、第３・四半期の利益成長が大幅に減速したと発表した。

玩具メーカー、ポップマートの業績不振もリスク回避姿勢を強めた。株価は２１日に５％下落。第３・四半期決算が失望視されるとと見込まれる中、今月１５％下げている。

市場関係者によると、投資家は第３・四半期の決算発表を前に、消費関連株の売買を通じて中国国内需要の弱さに対する弱気の見方を示している。経済成長が引き続き堅調な中、政策当局が早期に市場刺激策を打ち出す公算は小さいとみられている。

バークレイズはリポートで、輸出主導の産業が堅調なため引き続き内需の弱さを覆い隠していると指摘。「成長目標がほぼ達成されており、大規模な景気刺激策導入のハードルは高まったとみている」との見方を示した。

酒類と新エネルギー関連企業が下げを主導した一方、医薬品、通信、クラウドコンピューティング関連企業は相場をアウトパフォームした。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、ソフィー・アルターマット氏はリポートで「政府の焦点は、短期的な成長押し上げよりも、技術進歩、産業の高度化、自給率の一段の向上に引き続き置かれている」と指摘した。

市場関係者によると、短期的にはより厳格な税制政策も株式相場の重しとなっている。

ロイターの報道によると、中国政府は富裕層に対し、海外信託関連の所得税を１０月２２日までに申告・納税するよう求めた。これを受け、現金確保のため株式を売却する動きが一部で広がっている。

小型株中心の深セン総合指数は０．４９％安、新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．６２％下落、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は０．０６％高。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず 焦点：ＳＨＥＩＮの香港上場、ＥＳＧ問題がなお影　投資家の懸念根強く 最終更新: 10/21(水) 19:08 ロイター

item.title: Turkey plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
item.description: Turkey will submit to parliament a mandate allowing for military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey will submit to parliament a mandate allowing for military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party told Reuters on Wednesday. The lawmaker, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the mandate would be sent to parliament once a bill ratifying the accord has been approved. Turkey [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"submitted"] the [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] — signed by the three countries in August — to parliament for ratification on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks. The AKP lawmaker said that no Turkish troops deployed to other countries under the pact would take part in offensive operations, adding that technical personnel and experts would be sent initially to help with air defences, electronic warfare technologies, and other defensive support. Earlier, two officials had told Reuters that [USN:L6N45T0WB TEXT:"Turkey's contribution"] was expected to be limited to military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far. Turkey, which has condemned the Houthi attacks, has also agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

item.title: Elevance lifts 2026 profit forecast on lower medical costs, higher premiums
item.description: Elevance Health on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results due to higher premiums and lower medical costs, driving the health insurer's shares 2.1% higher in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elevance Health (ELV.N) on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results due to higher premiums and lower medical costs, driving the health insurer's shares 2.1% higher in premarket trading. Health insurers have been grappling with declining membership, as well as rising costs from elevated demand for behavioral health services and specialty drugs in government-backed plans. Elevance, like other health insurers, has adjusted its pricing to reflect higher medical costs. For the third quarter, the company said higher premium yields and service fees offset lower membership, helping the company's insurance business post a $1.1 billion rise in revenue from a year earlier. Last week, larger rival UnitedHealth Group (UNH.N) also raised its full-year profit forecast, attributing the improvement to plan design and new pricing on products. Elevance's upbeat quarterly performance reflects "stronger execution across our diversified portfolio and underscore the earnings power of the business," CEO Gail K. Boudreaux said. Medical membership of about 44.9 million as of September 30 decreased by 487,000 compared to the prior year, the company said. For the third quarter, the health insurer reported a medical loss ratio, the percentage of premiums spent on medical care, of 90.6%, lower than analysts' expectations of 91.17%. The company said lower costs were due to better performance in its Medicare Advantage plans for older Americans and those with disabilities as well as Obamacare plans compared to the prior year. The company also said it plans to deliver at least 12% growth in 2027 adjusted profit from an earnings baseline of at least $26.75 per share. Elevance forecast full-year adjusted profit to be at least $29 per share, compared with its previous outlook of at least $27 per share. Analysts on average estimate an annual profit of $27.23 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. On an adjusted basis, the company earned a profit of $6.99 per share, compared with analysts' average estimate of $4.68 per share.

item.title: How the Republican redistricting gambit faltered under Trump slump
item.description: Nine Republican-redrawn districts now lean Democratic or are too close to call.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: At President Donald Trump 's urging, Republicans pursued an unprecedented mid-decade redistricting campaign ahead of November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], redrawing dozens of US House of Representatives districts in an effort to preserve their narrow majority. With less than two weeks until Election Day, however, Trump's unpopularity has wiped out most of those gains, leaving Republicans scrambling to defend even districts they engineered to be safely conservative. As of June, Republicans had increased their advantage in 16 redrawn districts. Today, nine of those Republican-leaning districts are either expected to go to Democrats or are too close to call, according to a Reuters analysis of ratings from leading election forecasters. A 10th Republican district was thrown out by courts. Redistricting typically occurs only once a decade following the US Census' population count. But Texas Republicans tore up the state's existing US House map last summer with Trump's backing, setting off a multistate fight between the parties that Republicans [USN:L1N4250NA TEXT:"appeared to win"] handily. Democrats were only able to use redistricting to gain an edge in six districts. But what looked like a Republican victory has since been undercut by Trump's record-low approval rating, driven by the unpopular war in Iran and Americans' deep frustration with the resulting high gas prices. "It's a powerful lesson that you can be too smart for your own good when you try to predict the future," said Michael Li, a redistricting expert at New York University's Brennan Center for Justice. TEXAS, FLORIDA RACES NO LONGER SAFE BETS Most of the Republican gains were expected to come from Texas and Florida, where new maps reshaped nine Democratic-held seats into districts that Trump carried in 2024 by anywhere from 9 to 20 percentage points. But the collapse of Trump's support among Latino voters has upended the political calculus in those states. Analysts now view only one of those nine as a sure thing for Republicans, with six considered highly competitive. "I think the maps in Texas and Florida were way too confident that Hispanic voters would continue to vote for Republicans at the same level they did in 2024," said Erin Covey, who analyzes US House races for the Cook Political Report. "There is absolutely a world where Republicans don't flip any of the four seats they redrew in Florida." The median outcome for Republicans is a gain of around three seats from redistricting alone, Covey said. But if the Democratic wave turns into a tsunami, she added, Democrats could actually end up netting two seats through redistricting. That said, the national House map is objectively better for Republicans than it was prior to redistricting, according to Jacob Rubashkin, an analyst at Inside Elections. "The number of pickups is almost certain to fall well below expectation," he said. "It's also true that Republicans will still do better because they redistricted than had they lived and let live." Some of the newly redrawn districts are among the races that have drawn the most campaign spending, underscoring their competitiveness. Four of the six House races that have received the most outside spending from Republican-aligned groups - an average of more than $12 million each - are taking place in Republican-redistricted seats, according to campaign finance data. Democrats need to flip at least four House seats on November 3 to win control of the chamber. DEMOCRATS REACH DEEP INTO REPUBLICAN TERRITORY Even districts that once seemed unassailable are [USN:L6N45T19V TEXT:"potentially in reach"] for Democrats. After the US Supreme Court in April [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"hollowed out"] the Voting Rights Act's protections for districts with large minority populations, Alabama Republicans quickly dismantled one of the state's two predominantly Black districts in favor of a new, majority-white one that backed Trump by more than 14 percentage points in 2024. But now, two national forecasters, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia, both categorize the race as "Lean Republican," suggesting incumbent Democrat Shomari Figures could prevail in a strong Democratic wave. To be sure, Democrats may not carry every seat they redrew either. In California, where Democratic lawmakers passed a new map targeting five Republican-held seats, two Republicans are locked in tight contests with Democratic challengers, according to analysts. In some cases, the new maps could also have unintended consequences for incumbent Republicans. Under the updated Texas map, the seat of Republican Monica De La Cruz remained solidly Republican, with Trump winning the district's voters by nearly 18 percentage points. But most of that territory was new to her, forcing the incumbent to introduce herself to swaths of new voters. Her Democratic opponent, Bobby Pulido, is a well-known Tejano music star who has sought to transform his cultural popularity into political success. That seat is now widely seen as a tossup.

item.title: End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal
item.description: London-based Cai Baochun used to make a hefty profit reselling Hermes' famed Birkin bags for more than double their $10,000 retail price. Now he has stopped stockpiling them as second-hand prices fall.
item.dc:creator: Tassilo Hummel, Helen Reid, Alessandro Parodi
item.content:encoded: London-based Cai Baochun used to make a hefty profit reselling Hermes' (HRMS.PA) famed Birkin bags for more than double their $10,000 retail price. Now he has stopped stockpiling them as second-hand prices fall. “I don’t want to lose money,” said Cai, who started selling the bags on online platforms such as Vestiaire Collective and on social media in 2020 and rode a pandemic-era luxury spending boom. The resale value of unworn Birkins sold as second-hand online has dropped by more than $6,000 from its 2022 peak, he said. The decline reflects a broader shift in the market for one of luxury's most exclusive products whose appeal and success have been driven by scarcity. Increasing supply of Birkin bags in the second-hand market is depressing resale premiums, according to resellers, industry consultants and analysts interviewed by Reuters, raising questions about a strategy that helped propel Hermes to become one of the world's most profitable luxury companies. Named after the late British-French actor Jane Birkin, the handbag has been central to Hermes' performance. Between 2015 and 2025, group annual sales tripled to €16 billion ($18 billion) while its market value surged. Last year, Hermes posted an operating margin of 41%, above that of rivals including Chanel, Kering-owned Gucci and LVMH's leather and fashion division, which includes Louis Vuitton and Dior. RESALE MARKET UNDER PRESSURE All of that was underpinned by an aura of exclusivity. Six resellers who source bags directly from Hermes shoppers said access to a Birkin is generally linked to spending on Hermes scarves, clothes and shoes, although the exact policy differs between regions and stores. Two estimated customers typically spend $10,000 to $20,000 before being offered the Birkin or the Kelly, the brand's other popular bag. Hermes, which says a Birkin takes 15 hours to craft, does not disclose its selling policies or how many bags it makes. It declined to comment for this story. Of the nine Birkin resellers Reuters interviewed in the US, Europe and Asia, six said resale prices had fallen over the past year as more handbags became available, while five reported softer demand. Antoinette Hunter, who founded luxury handbag reseller Lilac Blue in 2007, said when she got the first request for a Birkin, few people knew the bag. She eventually sourced one from a member of Japan’s royal family. Acquiring Birkins is no longer a challenge, Hunter said, but it's harder to make money from resales. She said the price for an unworn black Birkin 25 bag, one of the most sought-after models, has fallen by around £4,000 ($5,336) since 2022, to around £24,000. Cai, who sells via Vestiaire Collective and Instagram, says his price for the bag is around £20,000. Hermes sells the same model for £9,390 in Britain, a Hermes sales assistant in London said. Although Hunter still sees plenty of demand for Hermès bags, particularly the most high-end ones, she said the decline in resale prices might dissuade some from buying directly from Hermes. "If Hermes continues to raise the prices, and the prices on the resale market continue to drop, that margin gets squeezed, and perhaps it will become less appealing," she said. Brokerage Bernstein, which tracks individual auction results, said in a September note the resale price on Birkin 25 bags averaged about 1.7 times the retail tag in the third quarter, down from about 2.6 times at their 2022 peak. BUSINESS MODEL UNDER SCRUTINY Hermes' leather goods division, which includes other handbag models, generates 44% of annual group revenue. For more than a decade, limited supply and strong demand allowed Birkins to command hefty resale premiums, benefiting both Hermes and resellers as the prospects of making a profit via the secondary market encouraged Hermes clients to buy more from the brand. "It was a win-win," said Sarah Davis, founder of California-based Fashionphile. The company said its Birkin listings have grown 32-fold in 15 years. The company's website currently lists 212 Birkins on sale. Hermes has gradually expanded the production of its handcrafted items, opening one workshop per year on average. Meanwhile, the rise of resale platforms such as Vestiaire Collective and The RealReal, alongside vintage boutiques with online shops and social media channels, has made it easier than ever to resell. The bags and other Hermes items remain highly sought after, resellers said, but the brand is showing some strain. Hermes’ shares have lost nearly 40% of their market value this year, making the brand one of the worst performers among listed luxury companies. Earlier this month, UBS analysts downgraded Hermes shares to "sell", saying that growing secondary-market supply of Birkins and Kellys could weaken the brand's scarcity-driven business model. "We believe the nature of the business is changing," they said in a note, estimating that the number of the handbags listed for sale worldwide is now six to seven times higher than before the pandemic. The company is expected to report quarterly sales growth of 5.2% on Thursday, which would mark its weakest quarterly growth in six years, according to Visible Alpha estimates. While leather goods revenue is still expected to grow by 10%, demand for clothing, silk scarves and perfumes is cooling, a sign fewer customers are making the purchases traditionally required to buy a Birkin at a later stage, two equities analysts and two industry consultants said. Asked in July whether Hermes should slow production to protect the brand, Hermes CEO Axel Dumas told reporters that some people feared making too many bags would hurt its exclusivity, while others questioned why it was not making more. He added that output depended largely on the number of fully trained artisans and available high-quality leather. Not all resellers see weakness. Davis said prices for the bag on the Fashionphile platform have remained firm and even risen slightly this year, pointing to renewed attention generated by Norwegian soccer star Erling Haaland's handbag collection. ($1 = 0.8911 euros)

item.title: US invokes rarely used torture law in revamped case against Maduro
item.description: Nicolas Maduro is one of just a handful of people to be charged in the US with violating a federal law criminalizing torture committed overseas, a Reuters review of court records found, as prosecutors seek to broaden their criminal case against the ousted Venezuelan president.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: Nicolas Maduro is one of just a handful of people to be charged in the US with violating a federal law criminalizing [USN:L6N45U13M TEXT:"torture"] committed overseas, a Reuters review of court records found, as prosecutors seek to broaden their criminal case against the ousted Venezuelan president. Maduro, 63, and his wife Cilia Flores, 70, [USN:L6N461121 TEXT:"pleaded not guilty"] last week to an expanded indictment accusing them of conspiring to torture political opponents to remain in power, in addition to the drug trafficking charges they already faced. They are scheduled to go on trial in June 2027. Maduro and Flores, captured in January during a US military raid in Caracas ordered by President Donald Trump , are just the seventh and eighth people Reuters identified who have been charged with violating a 1994 law criminalizing acts of torture. The law defines torture as an act intended to inflict severe physical or mental pain or suffering on a person in custody. Four people have been convicted under the statute, including members of paramilitary forces in [USN:JOE50902R TEXT:"Liberia"] and [USN:L4N3UE1C5 TEXT:"Gambia"], the head of a [USN:L1N45912B TEXT:"Syrian prison"] under ousted President Bashar al-Assad, and a US citizen who developed an [USN:L4N2UT3P3 TEXT:"illegal arms factory"] in Iraq. The Maduro case marks the first time the United States has prosecuted a head of state for allegedly authorizing the use of torture in their country, according to Michel Paradis, a partner at the Steptoe law firm. "This really is a landmark case," said Paradis, who previously represented detainees at the Guantanamo Bay US naval base. The torture charges mark a substantial shift in the focus of the case against Maduro and Flores. While they remain accused of abusing their power to [USN:L6N3ZT19O TEXT:"help drug traffickers"] and enrich themselves, the new charges mean that alleged human rights abuses during the political upheaval that often marked Maduro's 13 years in office will become central to the trial. 'A SIGNIFICANT ESCALATION' The torture charge could strengthen the hand of prosecutors by allowing them to tell a more comprehensive story about how Maduro allegedly employed a wide range of criminal activity to stay in power, and by enabling them to call more sympathetic witnesses, legal experts said. "The torture charge is really a significant escalation," said Artie McConnell, a former federal prosecutor focused on national security issues. "It puts these torture and political repression elements at the center of the government's theory," McConnell added, referring to the prosecution. Lawyers for Maduro did not respond to requests for comment. Mark Donnelly and Andres Sanchez, lawyers for Flores, said she is "completely innocent" of all charges. They said they would revise a motion they previously made to dismiss the indictment on the basis of [USN:L6N44U15Y TEXT:"sovereign immunity"] — protection from prosecution as the head of a sovereign country — to account for the new charges. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney's office, which brought the charges, declined to comment. COOPERATING WITNESSES The 1994 law was passed by Congress to make good on US obligations under the United Nations Convention against Torture, signed during President Ronald Reagan's tenure. Under the law, each torture count is punishable by up to 20 years in prison, or by a life sentence or the death penalty if the victim dies due to the torture. People convicted of multiple acts of torture can receive longer sentences. Those convicted under the statute so far have received prison sentences of 60 to 97 years. Maduro and Flores are not eligible for the death penalty because they are charged with torture conspiracy, not with carrying out torture themselves. US prosecutors can bring torture charges only against defendants who are US nationals or who are physically present in the United States. The charges against Maduro and Flores came after they were brought to New York following the raid in Caracas. Many of the other defendants in US torture cases had moved to or attempted to enter the United States after the alleged torture. McConnell, a partner at law firm BakerHostetler, said the new indictment was more detailed than the previous one, citing the descriptions of alleged torture victims and incidents. In one 2018 incident described in the indictment, prosecutors said Venezuelan military officers hit a detainee with a machete and sprayed him with a chemical irritant while interrogating him about the whereabouts of a Maduro political opponent. Jurors could find testimony from alleged torture victims to be powerful, said Shane Stansbury, a former federal prosecutor in Manhattan. Three of the alleged torture victims in the indictment are American citizens, and their testimony could resonate particularly strongly among the jurors, McConnell said. A trial on the drug trafficking charges alone likely would have relied heavily on the testimony of cooperating witnesses, who may have played a role in the alleged crimes themselves. Defense lawyers often question cooperating witnesses sharply about their own criminal histories on cross-examination to try to undercut their credibility. To be sure, cooperating witnesses are still likely to prove critical in helping prosecutors link Maduro and Flores to the alleged torture, experts said. Kevin Sullivan, a prosecutor with the Manhattan US Attorney's office, said in an October 8 court hearing that cooperating witnesses would testify about alleged involvement by Maduro and Flores in the torture conspiracy. ACQUITTAL IN TENNESSEE Not every torture case the US has brought has resulted in a conviction. One defendant, an upstate New York resident named Sulejman Mujagic who was charged in the US in 2012 with torturing a soldier after the breakup of the former Yugoslavia, was instead extradited to Bosnia for trial in 2013. Another defendant charged over alleged torture in Bosnia, Sead Miljkovic, was found not guilty of US torture charges by a jury in Chattanooga, Tennessee, in 2025 but later pleaded guilty to passport fraud. He has since left the US, according to his lawyer, Bryan Hoss. Hoss said the accounts given by the alleged victims who testified in the case had shifted over time, undercutting their credibility, and that the abuse allegedly committed by his client did not rise to the level of torture. Hoss also said that jurors may have questioned why the US government was prosecuting the case. Jurors in the Maduro trial may not have similar concerns. "The fact that these are filed against the former head of the country allows people to understand it a little better," Hoss said.

item.description: BRUSSELS, Oct 21 : EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday.The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition

FAST

BRUSSELS, Oct 21 : EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday. The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years. Big online platforms are required to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their sites under the bloc's Digital Services Act, or risk fines of as much as 6 per cent of their global annual turnover for violations. Booking.com said it was engaging constructively with the Commission. "Security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities at Booking.com," a spokesperson for the company said.

"We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud, and protect travelers and partners." The EU investigation will focus on fake listings — such as for non-existent properties — impersonation fraud and non-compliant accommodation offers, and whether Booking.com has properly identified, assessed and mitigated the systemic risks related to these. Regulators will also look into phishing scams exploiting Booking.com's reservation and guest data shared with accommodation providers, the Commission said. A third element will be paid-for boosted listings not clearly identifiable as advertisements. Booking.com is part of Booking Holdings. "Europeans should be able to book their holidays without fear of being scammed," EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement. "The Digital Services Act sets clear responsibilities on platforms to address these risks, and we must ensure that the leading booking platform in Europe takes those responsibilities seriously," she said.

item.title: 中国奇瑞、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向き＝幹部
item.description: [蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] - 中国の自動車大手、奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の幹部は２１日、米自動車メーカーとの提...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国奇瑞、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向き＝幹部 19:02 配信

2026年10月12日、パリのオートショーに展示された奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の車。 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

[蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] - 中国の自動車大手、奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の幹部は２１日、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向きな姿勢を示した。「オモダ」「ジェクー」ブランドを展開する同社は欧州などで急成長しており、今後は北米での事業拡大を目指す。

バイスプレジデントのチャーリー・チャン氏は中国東部・蕪湖の本社でインタビューに応じ、２０２７年初めにカナダでブランドを立ち上げる準備を進めていることも明らかにした。

米国では１００％を超える関税やデータセキュリティー規制が障壁となり、中国の自動車メーカーは事実上締め出されている。

チャン氏は「米国については当然さまざまな選択肢を探っている」と述べ、柔軟に対応する姿勢を強調した。「米自動車メーカーとの提携の可能性も含め、さまざまな選択肢に非常に前向きだ」と語った。具体的にどのような提携を想定しているかは明らかにしなかった。

「技術面ではハードウエアもソフトウエアも中国製に頼らない方法を確実に見いだせる」と述べ、米国市場への参入に道筋をつけられるとの自信を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：トヨタの中国合弁2社に再編機運、市場縮小と競争激化で転換点 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 焦点：中国車メーカー、カナダ進出に本腰　米市場開放にらみ「予行演習」 コラム：中国車の米市場参入は時間の問題 アングル：中国自動車メーカーが欧州で最も勢力を伸ばした地域 最終更新: 10/21(水) 19:02 ロイター

item.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 21 : As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology. OpenAI’s safety practices have been in the spotlight in rec

OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 21 : As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology.  OpenAI’s safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US President Donald Trump’s voluntary AI safety agreement on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways." Yet Leading the Future, a political group backed with a $25 million donation from Brockman and his wife, Anna, opposes regulations that “unduly constrain or delay AI development” in the US. The group is spending millions to influence the outcome of at least 48 races for US House and Senate seats.  INDUSTRY PROFITS VERSUS REGULATION

Brockman’s backing prompted criticism from AI safety advocates, who say it raises questions about whether OpenAI executives genuinely want the US government to impose requirements on powerful AI systems. Federal government requirements could hurt the industry's profits if they slow the release of new models or prompt the companies to change how their products perform to address security concerns. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are laying the groundwork for public offerings that are expected to rank among the largest ever. “There are leaders in industry who want to pay lip service to regulation because they realize where public opinion is,” said Charlie Blaettler of Guardrails Alliance, a political group formed to counter Leading the Future. “But they're the same leaders who stood up a super PAC whose sole purpose was to oppose candidates who stand up for regulation.” OpenAI said in a blog post that the Brockmans' donation was in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the company. Greg Brockman's personal spokesperson declined to comment on his donations. In a post on X from 2025, Brockman said that "being pro-AI does not mean being anti-regulation. It means being thoughtful."  Leading the Future’s spokesperson, Jesse Hunt, did not address the donation in a statement, saying the group seeks "champions who can work together in Congress to advance a strong, responsible national regulatory AI framework." The New York Times reported in September that the Brockmans backed out of a pledge to donate another $25 million to Leading the Future. Leading the Future declined to comment on the New York Times' reporting.  FEDERAL LAW TO PRE-EMPT STATE AI LAWS Other contributors to Leading the Future include Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, who, along with their venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, gave a combined $50 million to the group, according to Federal Election Commission records. Andreessen Horowitz is an investor in OpenAI.  One of the candidates Leading the Future is backing is Republican Andy Barr, who is running to represent Kentucky in the Senate. Barr told the newspaper the Lexington Herald-Leader in March that he supports federal legislation that would block individual states from passing or enforcing their own regulations on AI, a concept known as pre-emption. Build American AI, a nonprofit group affiliated with Leading the Future, has run advertisements on social media platforms calling on Congress to pass a national standard for AI, rather than allowing states to pass their own rules. Leading the Future also sent funds to Republicans Julia Letlow, who is running for Senate in Louisiana, and Amanda McKinney, a candidate for Congress in Washington state. Both say on their campaign websites that they are opposed to "heavy-handed" regulation of the AI sector. OpenAI rival Anthropic has given at least $40 million to Public First Action, a political action committee that is against federal pre-emption laws. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called federal pre-emption of state rules "too blunt".

Source: Reuters

item.title: Shark nicknamed 'Bukangi' returns to sea off South Korea after third rescue attempt
item.description: A shark that became a sensation after spending more than a month in a canal in the South Korean port of Busan was successfully guided back into the open sea on Wednesday, following two failed rescue attempts, the oceans ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Hyun Yi, Daewoung Kim
item.content:encoded: A shark that became a sensation after spending more than a month in a canal in the South Korean port of Busan was successfully guided back into the open sea on Wednesday, following two failed rescue attempts, the oceans ministry said. The shark, nicknamed "Bukangi", was first spotted in a narrow waterway on September 18. More than 1.6 million people visited the waterfront park through October 20 to catch a glimpse of it, according to the Busan Infrastructure Corporation. Lee Min-jeung, a 39-year-old travel content creator from Seoul, said she had travelled to Busan four times to see Bukangi. "I'm relieved that it seems to have returned to the sea," Lee said. "Goodbye. Don't get sick." South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science identified Bukangi as a female dusky shark measuring about 3 meters (10 feet) in length. WARMING WATERS COULD BE BEHIND SIGHTINGS The species, which inhabits tropical, subtropical and temperate waters, is classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Bukangi's appearance has also drawn attention to changes in the waters around South Korea, with experts citing warming seas as one possible factor behind a rise in large shark sightings. The fisheries institute recorded 46 sightings of large sharks along the country's east coast in the first half of this year, compared with 12 during the same period last year. The shark's stay was unusual because the narrow canal lies near high-rise buildings and a major high-speed rail station in central Busan. The operation to free it was deemed necessary because the shark had not been observed feeding, and falling temperatures could affect its health, city officials said. South Korean media also said Bukangi had sustained minor injuries to its fin and snout. Authorities tried to guide it out on September 29 and October 2 but both attempts were unsuccessful. On Wednesday, authorities used a net attached to floating platforms and divers to navigate the canal's underwater terrain and varying depths. Workers moved the net toward the sea while preventing the shark from swimming back into the canal.

item.title: Putin hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks, frees US citizen held in Russia
item.description: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US school teacher who had been held in Russia on mercenary charges, has been released.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Putin hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks, frees US citizen held in Russia

Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US school teacher who had been held in Russia on mercenary charges, has been released.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev greets US special envoy Steve Witkoff upon his arrival at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, Russia on Oct 21, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)

FAST

ST PETERSBURG, Russia: President Vladimir Putin hosted US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in a grand imperial palace on Wednesday (Oct 21) to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two. The talks in St Petersburg , the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of a retired US school teacher held in Russia. The encounter comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications. The latest talks came more than two years since US President Donald Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.

Witkoff flew into Russia's second city on Wednesday morning a day after conducting what a US official called "constructive" talks in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the leaders of Finland and Norway and European and NATO representatives, as President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections. Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system , though Zelenskyy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo, Norway on Oct 20, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/NTB/Heiko Junge)

STARLINK SPEEDS Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday that the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Witkoff's meeting with Zelenskyy was positive and that Witkoff would share the results with Russia. He also reiterated that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink. "He will now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress," he said.

Related:

Zelenskyy hails resumption of US advance warning of strikes on Ukraine

Ukraine claims US missile holdup ahead of reported talks

TRUMP PRESSURE Despite the apparently cordial nature of Tuesday's meeting in Oslo, Trump, as he showed in comments in the White House on Tuesday, remains frustrated with Zelenskyy, whom he has repeatedly rebuked and suggested needs to be replaced. "He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," Trump told reporters on the eve of the talks in Russia. Putin, who has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and no NATO membership for Kyiv, will receive Witkoff in the Constantine Palace, a grand imperial edifice in what is the Kremlin chief's home city. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy and his main point man for potential economic and financial deals with the US, would also be present at the meeting with Witkoff, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said. A US official said Ukraine had brought new ideas and proposals to the Oslo talks, which had made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging with Russia. The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework", including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture. Witkoff would aim to "create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations," the official said. Zelenskyysaid he hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump. The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskyy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile and that a lot of the legwork required for an overall agreement would need to be in place. Trump said on Tuesday he had raised the idea with Putin of freeing Stephen Hubbard - a 74-year-old retired US school teacher being held in Russia on mercenary charges he denies. Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard was at the airport waiting to fly back to the United States with him. Witkoff thanked Putin for the goodwill gesture. Hubbard was first detained in April 2022 and was later sentenced to six years and 10 months on charges whose veracity his family and US-based lawyer question.

Source: Reuters/nh

item.title: イラク、イランとの国境検問所を閉鎖 治安状況確認中＝関係筋
item.description: [バスラ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バスラ ２１日 ロイター] - イラクの国境当局者は２１日、イランとの国境にある交通量の多いシーブ検問所を閉鎖し、治安状況の評価や、禁止物品の密輸を阻止するための検査装置の設置を行っていると述べた。

同検問所の他の関係筋２人によると、追って通知があるまで、乗客、車両、商用トラックの通行が禁止される。

イラクは９月、サウジアラビアに対するドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けた予防措置として、イランとのもう一つの国境検問所であるシャラムチェの閉鎖を命令。サウジ当局は、ドローンがイラクから発射されたと主張していた。

イラクの国境検問所当局者はロイターに対し、シーブ検問所における現在の治安対策は脆弱で不十分だと語った。

item.title: Russia says it will send first diesel cargo to US on Thursday
item.description: Russia will dispatch its first tanker with diesel for the United States on Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, according to the Vedomosti news outlet, after a deal with US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia will dispatch its first tanker with diesel for the United States on Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, according to the Vedomosti news outlet, after a deal with US President Donald Trump. Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports on October 9, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"reaching the deal"] with Trump to supply diesel to global markets. Novak said on Wednesday the vessel will carry 40,000 metric tons of the fuel, adding that the paperwork on the fuel supply is nearing its completion, according to media reports. He did not name the port from which the cargo will be delivered. "Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities," RIA news agency quoted Novak as saying. Trump has said Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter". The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L6N4670LA TEXT:"was hosting"] US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday, after the US-Russia diesel export deal led to a sharp deterioration in ties between the United States and Ukraine. During the talks in St Petersburg, Witkoff thanked Putin for lifting the export restrictions. Putin also mentioned the deal, saying that global diesel prices dropped by 5%-6% after the agreement. "That's an example of us working together, I want to thank you for that," Witkoff said in televised comments. Putin also said that first Russian tankers with diesel will departs in two to three days. "We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided," he said, adding that Russia also would be able to supply fertilisers in "large quantities" to the US market.

item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 ２１日 ロイター] - ラピダス（東京都千代田区）の東哲郎会長は ２１日、来...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ラピダス、2ナノ量産「ほぼ計画通り」　当初の顧客は米中心に＝会長 18:42 配信

ラピダスのロゴ。2026年8月21日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato/File Photo

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２１日 ロイター] - ラピダス（東京都千代田区）の東哲郎会長は ２１日、来年後半の量産を目指す回路線幅２ナノメートル（ナノは１０億分の１）の半導体について、量産に向け「ほぼオンスケジュール」で進んでいると述べた。課題となる顧客獲得に関し、当初は人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の需要がある米国が中心になるとの見通しを示した。

都内で講演し、来場者との質疑で語った。日本国内でも、コンピューター関連企業などへの半導体提供に向けた協議が進展しているとした。その上で「今後、非常にマーケットが広がっていくので、それほど心配していない」と話した。

また、ラピダスの工場がある北海道千歳市に関し、台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が進出した熊本県を念頭に「九州を真似するわけではないが、サイエンスパークのようなものを形成していこうということで非常に活発に動いていて、われわれも一緒にやっていこうと考えている」と語った。

item.title: Yemen's Houthis deny launching drones towards Saudi Arabia's Medina
item.description: Yemen's Houthis said that they had neither launched drones towards the Saudi holy city of Medina on Wednesday nor conducted military operations towards Saudi Arabia, refuting earlier comments from the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis said that they had neither launched drones towards the Saudi holy city of Medina on Wednesday nor conducted military operations towards Saudi Arabia, refuting earlier comments from the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen. The comments by the Iran-aligned group's military spokesperson Yahya Saree follow the coalition saying that it had intercepted drones over Medina and the Eastern region. The Houthis had warned airlines this month against using the Saudi airspace as they intensified attacks on the kingdom, the world's largest oil exporter, saying only the airspace over Islam's holy cities of Mecca and Medina would be exempted. The Houthis have attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and state oil giant [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], disrupting flights and oil exports. Yemen, one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, has been mired in a civil war since 2014 when the Houthis drove the government out of the northern capital, drawing Saudi-led military intervention. Renewed fighting in recent weeks ended a 2022 UN-brokered truce that had largely halted cross-border attacks between a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthis, who controls the capital Sanaa. The escalation has opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . Within Yemen, the Houthis claimed an attack on Wednesday on a military camp near the airport in the southern city of Aden, where the Yemeni government is based. A government military source and a local official told Reuters the group also attacked Riyan airport in the southeastern coastal city of Mukalla. A Houthi missile attack on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province on Monday [USN:L1N4660GJ TEXT:"killed 73 people"].

FAST

Oct 21 : Netflix shares dropped 6 per cent in premarket trading on Wednesday after the company cut its full-year advertising forecast and issued a tepid fourth-quarter profit outlook, deepening concerns about slowing viewership and revenue growth. The stock has declined more than 26 per cent this year and, if current losses hold, the streaming giant is set to shed about $17 billion of its market value. The share performance underscores the mounting challenges facing Netflix, from losing a bidding war for Warner Bros Discovery earlier this year to defending its paid subscription model against free digital rivals and competing in an increasingly consolidated streaming market. As viewers shift toward free, user-generated platforms such as YouTube and TikTok, Netflix is also contending with changing preferences in favor of short-form video over premium content.

"Netflix is still the leader in streaming, but the competitive landscape for people's attention is much broader than streaming alone, particularly with the growth of short-form video," said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot. The company needs to ensure its content remains compelling enough to keep viewers engaged, rather than simply retaining them as subscribers, Barringer said. Netflix is also undergoing a restructuring after cutting about 6 per cent of its workforce and reshuffling its leadership team this month. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said on Tuesday the company plans to focus on its core business of producing quality TV shows and movies to make Netflix a must-have service, and the recent executive shakeup was a step toward that goal. At least 14 brokerages have lowered their price targets on the stock after the results, according to data compiled by LSEG. Netflix trades at nearly 18.28 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 14.76 times for Walt Disney and 6.26 times for Comcast, underscoring the premium investors place on the streaming giant.

Source: Reuters

item.content:encoded:
グラブのフードパンダ台湾事業買収、当局が認めず　競争懸念で 18:36 配信

配車・配達サービス会社グラブのロゴ。2026年2月25日、シンガポールで撮影。 REUTERS/Edgar Su

[台北 ２１日 ロイター] - 台湾の公平交易委員会（公正取引委員会）は２１日、競争上の懸念を理由に、シンガポールのグラブによるフードパンダの台湾宅配事業買収を認めなかったと発表した。

東南アジア最大の配車・配達サービス会社グラブは３月、フードパンダの台湾宅配事業を現金６億ドルで買収すると発表していた。グラブにとって東南アジア域外への初進出となる計画だった。

公平交易委員会は、買収によって生じる競争への悪影響が経済全体への利益を上回ると判断した。フードパンダを傘下に置く独料理宅配デリバリーヒーローとグラブの両社が確約した条件についても「競争上の懸念を解消するには不十分」とした。

item.description: [フランクフルト ２１日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のエコノミストらは２１日のブログで、ユーロ圏経済は今...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏、ＡＩとグリーン経済がエネショック緩和＝ＥＣＢブログ 18:28 配信

[フランクフルト ２１日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のエコノミストらは２１日のブログで、ユーロ圏経済は今年のエネルギーショックを予想以上にうまく乗り切っており、化石燃料への依存度低下、財政支援強化、そしてＡＩ（人工知能）投資ブームが成長の維持に寄与していると述べた。

域内経済について、現在の石油依存度は１９９０年代初頭に比べて約半分に低下しており、エネルギー価格ショックの影響が限定的になっていると推定。ＡＩ関連の貿易がユーロ圏にとって「重要な追い風」となっており、技術関連の輸出受注やＡＩ関連セクターが好調に推移していると指摘した。

一方で、財政刺激策といった支援の多くが一時的なものにとどまる可能性があると警告。世界的な需要、財政刺激策、ＡＩ投資が後退すれば、地政学的緊張が悪化したり、エネルギー市場で新たな混乱が生じたりした場合、ユーロ圏は脆弱な立場に置かれることになる。

item.title: Trump envoy asks Putin to resume three-way Ukraine peace talks, secures release of US citizen
item.description: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to review new ideas on ending the war amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to consider resuming US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine and to review new ideas on ending the war amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two. The talks in a grand imperial palace in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard, a retired US school teacher"] held in Russia. Putin also offered to help US President Donald Trump in dealing with Iran, saying Russia had a decades-long relationship with Tehran which it has repeatedly offered to leverage to address US concerns about Iran's nuclear programme. Russia could also supply large quantities of fertiliser to the United States to help US farmers, the Russian president told Witkoff, saying he wanted to discuss [USN:L1N4650BJ TEXT:"a potential meeting in China next month"] with Trump which the Kremlin has suggested could also include Chinese President Xi Jinping. The encounter comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications. The latest talks also come more than two years since Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours. "One thing that I hope to accomplish today is to have some good conversation between us about the resumption potentially of trilateral talks between Ukraine and Russia and the United States," Witkoff told Putin. "Even if we don't have a resolution today, if we just talk about and sort of consider what that next step might be I think that would be important and the world is waiting to hear that". The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran . Ukraine and Russia remain far apart when it comes to the terms of any possible peace deal, but Trump has recently intensified pressure on Ukraine to strike some kind of a deal. He said on Tuesday it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." 'NEW IDEAS' Putin, who has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and no NATO membership for Kyiv, received Witkoff in the Constantine Palace, a grand imperial edifice in what is the Kremlin chief's home city. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy, was also present at the meeting with Witkoff as both sides talked up the potential of post-war Russia-US economic cooperation. Witkoff flew into Russia's second city a day after conducting [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"talks"] in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the leaders of Finland and Norway and European and NATO representatives. Witkoff said he would brief Putin on the Oslo talks which he described as productive and said had been characterised by "some degree of momentum." He said he had brought some documents with him containing various ideas for a potential peace deal for Putin to review, and that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, also wanted to convey some ideas to Putin and would shortly join the meeting remotely by phone. A US official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Ukraine had brought [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"new ideas and proposals"] to the Oslo talks, which had made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging with Russia. The official said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework," including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture. Zelenskiy said he hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump. The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskiy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile. FRAYING US-UKRAINE TIES US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections. Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskiy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues. Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated on Wednesday that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.

item.title: 豪データセンターＮＥＸＴＤＣ、新規開発凍結 時価総額ほぼ半減
item.description:
Scott Murdoch Rajasik Mukherjee
[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
豪データセンターＮＥＸＴＤＣ、新規開発凍結　時価総額ほぼ半減 18:15 配信

データセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣのロゴ。2026年6月22日、シドニーで撮影。 REUTERS/Hollie Adams

Scott Murdoch　Rajasik Mukherjee

[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデータセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣの株価が２１日急落し、時価総額がほぼ半減した。今後１年間の売上高見通しを大幅に引き下げ、開発計画を凍結すると発表したことが響いた。

同社によると、メルボルンの主要プロジェクトの一つで電力網の増強が遅れており、今年度に計上する予定だった売上高約１億４０００万豪ドル（９８００万米ドル）が先送りされる。ＮＥＸＴＤＣは当面、新規開発プロジェクトと用地取得を全て凍結すると説明した。

株価は４１．７％安で取引を終え、時価総額が約３０億豪ドル減少した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）に対する投資家心理はここ数週間で悪化している。急増する計算処理や用地、電力のコストに見合う成果を生むのかを巡り、巨額のＡＩ投資に疑問が広がっている。オーストラリアでは先週、データセンター企業が新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を撤回した。データセンター株やハイテク株が売られ、クレジット投資家はＡＩ関連企業への投資を一段と厳しく選別するようになっている。

ＮＥＸＴＤＣは２０２７年の純売上高を４億７５００万─５億豪ドルと見込む。従来予想の６億１５００万─６億４０００万豪ドルから引き下げた。調整後ＥＢＩＴＤＡ（利払い・税金・償却前利益）予想も、３億８５００万─４億１０００万豪ドルから２億４５００万─２億６５００万豪ドルに引き下げた。いずれも電力網増強の遅れで影響を受ける契約分を除いた数字だ。

同社によると、配電会社ジェメナ・エレクトリシティ・ネットワークスによる工事の遅れで、メルボルンのＭ３データセンターへの次の電力供給拡大は２０２８年になる見通しだ。

ジェメナは地域住民や関係者の反対を受け、Ｍ３への電力供給の増強に必要な電力網工事の一部を中断している。再開は早くても２７年２月になるとみている。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ルノー、ＥＶ新会社ＩＰＯ中止は「災い転じて福」か コラム：ビットコインＥＴＦ初承認、実用化拡大はなお遠い アングル：来年のＩＰＯ回復に期待、米利下げ観測が追い風 アングル：中国ユニツリー、上場後に株価急落　バブルやＩＰＯ制度に懸念 焦点：ＳＨＥＩＮの香港上場、ＥＳＧ問題がなお影　投資家の懸念根強く 最終更新: 10/21(水) 18:15 ロイター

Oct 21 : Super Micro Computer jumped over 12 per cent on Wednesday after it forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin comfortably above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI data center demand remains resilient. Shares of the AI server maker rose 12.2 per cent to $36.44 in premarket trading. FAST

TAIPEI: Taiwan's Fair Trade Commission said on Wednesday (Oct 21) it had blocked Grab's purchase of Delivery Hero's Foodpanda delivery business in Taiwan, citing competition concerns. Grab, Southeast Asia's biggest ride-hailing and delivery firm, said in March it would pay US$600 million in cash for the Foodpanda delivery business in Taiwan, in its first expansion outside the region. The Fair Trade Commission said the harm to competition from the proposed deal outweighed its overall economic benefits, and that the commitments offered by the companies were "insufficient to eliminate the competition concerns". Grab said it was disappointed by the decision.  "Grab's core business across Southeast Asia remains robust. We will continue to focus our capital and resources on executing our growth roadmap and empowering communities across our regional footprint." Delivery Hero said in a statement that under the terms of the transaction, it has appropriate deal protections, including a break fee arrangement, subject to certain conditions.

Source: Reuters/nh

item.title: HDFC Bank probe finds senior executives leaked secrets to outsiders
item.description: HDFC identified the executives during an internal investigation that began after some leaders grew concerned about the possibility of information being leaked ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Anto Antony An internal probe by HDFC Bank Ltd. — India’s largest by market value — found evidence that two senior executives disclosed confidential business strategies and possible market-sensitive information to outsiders, according to people familiar with the matter. The executives oversee certain key businesses and functions at the bank, according to the people, who asked not to be named discussing confidential matters.  HDFC identified the executives during an internal investigation that began after some leaders grew concerned about the possibility of information being leaked, the people said. The probe is still underway as the bank continues to examine whether the information was misused, the people said. An HDFC Bank spokesperson acknowledged an internal review, but didn’t comment on its findings or the executives involved. “In line with our policies, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts,” the spokesperson said by email. “Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete.” The bank said it was committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics and governance and takes reports of potential violations seriously. The review comes at a sensitive moment for HDFC Bank, which has a market value of about $115 billion and has spent three decades cultivating a reputation for conservative management, strong internal controls and consistent profitability. The lender is preparing for its first outsider chief executive following boardroom disputes and management departures. Its share price has declined about 28% this year. The probe and its findings were reported to senior management, including some members of the board, earlier this year, the people said. Both executives have since been formally informed of the findings, and it wasn’t immediately clear what disciplinary action will be taken, the people said.  The findings add to the challenges confronting Anup Bagchi, a veteran of rival ICICI Group, who is set to become HDFC Bank’s chief executive on Oct. 27.  In recent months, internal divisions in HDFC have played out publicly. In March, then-chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences between his personal values and certain practices at the bank. An independent legal review commissioned by the lender subsequently said his concerns were not substantiated. Bagchi’s appointment follows the surprise decision of Sashidhar Jagdishan, the incumbent chief executive, not to seek another term. Jagdishan is stepping down after six years at the helm.  Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director and one of the bank’s longest-serving executives, has also asked to leave at the end of December. Founded in 1994, as the country opened its financial sector to private competition, HDFC Bank grew into a preferred investment for international fund managers seeking exposure to India’s rising incomes and expanding consumer credit.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Rajveer Pardesi　Raphael Satter

[２１日 ロイター] - 広く使われているプログラミング言語ＰＨＰの開発者チームは２１日、深刻な脆弱性２件を修正するプログラムを公開すると発表した。欧州連合（ＥＵ）のサイバーセキュリティー当局は、修正を適用できない組織は影響を受けるウェブサイトを停止すべきだと警告した。

ＰＨＰはインターネット上で広く使われている。過去１日の間に、ＰＨＰで動くウェブサイトが深刻なサイバー攻撃で侵入される恐れがあるとの臆測が広がっていた。

サイバーセキュリティー企業ハントレスによると、ＰＨＰはウェブサイトの構築・管理やサーバーの共有サービス、管理画面などに幅広く使われているほか、ＰＨＰの使用を明示していない多くのソフトウエアも内部ではＰＨＰで動いている。

ＰＨＰの開発側はセキュリティーに関する告知で、２件の脆弱性はいずれも深刻度評価基準「ＣＶＳＳ ｖ４．０」で、最高１０点のうち９．２と評価されていると明らかにした。その上で「修正版が公開され次第、速やかに更新する」よう利用者に呼びかけた。

修正プログラムは２１日１４００ＧＭＴ（日本時間午後１１時）に公開する予定としている。

ＥＵ機関サイバーセキュリティーサービス（ＣＥＲＴ－ＥＵ）は２０日の勧告で、９．２という評価は、認証なしで外部からコードを実行される危険性を示すと説明した。影響を受けるシステムなどに直ちに修正プログラムを適用できるよう準備を求め、対応できない場合は影響を受けるサイトの停止を検討すべきだとした。

ウェブホスティング企業ゴーダディは、この脆弱性により、攻撃者がインターネット経由で対象サーバー上でコードを実行できる恐れがあると説明。データの窃取やウェブサイトの改ざん、システム全体の乗っ取りにつながる可能性があるとした。

item.title: Antitrust watchdog launches probe into Spain's Exolum over potential abuse
item.description: Spain's competition authority CNMC has opened sanctioning proceedings against Spanish energy logistics company Exolum over three suspected abuses of a dominant position, it said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain's competition authority CNMC has opened sanctioning proceedings against Spanish energy logistics company Exolum over three suspected abuses of a dominant position, it said on Wednesday. The CNMC is investigating Exolum's alleged imposition of excessive fees and its refusal to grant access to its transport and storage facilities to a competing third-party operator at the northeastern port of Tarragona. The potential abuses might have led to consumers facing successive price hikes, the CNMC said, adding that the conduct would have allowed Exolum to maintain high profit margins and strengthen its dominant position in a coastal area of significant economic importance. "A third competitor might have seen its right of access to Spain's only pipeline network for the transport of liquid hydrocarbons restricted and, consequently, its ability to compete in downstream markets," it added. Exolum said it will cooperate fully with the CNMC throughout the proceedings and that it will exercise its right to defend itself. The company said in a statement that it considers its prices reasonable and transparent, and that its conduct complies with competition law and regulations. "In fact, price changes for Exolum's main services have been below the rate of inflation every year for the past 25 years and have remained unchanged throughout the recent energy crisis," Exolum said. The watchdog has up to 24 months to resolve the investigation.

item.title: 米写真大手ゲッティが破産を正式申請、事業再編目指す
item.description: [２１日 ロイター] - 米写真・映像販売大手ゲッティイメージズは２１日、連邦破産法１１条（日本の民事再生法に相当）...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米写真大手ゲッティが破産を正式申請、事業再編目指す 16:56 配信

写真はレッドカーペットで撮影するフォトグラファー。2019年5月、仏カンヌで撮影。REUTERS/Jean-Paul Pelissier

[２１日 ロイター] - 米写真・映像販売大手ゲッティイメージズは２１日、連邦破産法１１条（日本の民事再生法に相当）の適用を正式に申請した。非公開化して事業を再編する計画を１週間以上前に明らかにしていた。

• 多額の負債と人工知能（ＡＩ）生成画像との競争激化が背景。同業シャッターストックとの合併計画が破談となったことを受けた。

• ゲッティによると、ゲッティ家関連会社およびコッホ・エクイティ・デベロップメントが再編後に同社の株式を１００％保有する。

• ゲッティは、再建計画の正式承認を得るためのプロセス期間中も通常通り事業を継続し、コンテンツ提供者、パートナー、顧客、従業員、ベンダーに何の影響も及ぼさないとしている。

• 年末までに再編を完了する見込み。

• デラウェア州破産裁判所への提出書類の中で、同社は資産および負債の推定額をいずれも１０億─１００億ドルの範囲と記載。

• ゲッティは、コッホ・エクイティ・デベロップメントからの最大１億４３００万ドルの資金が再編プロセスを支えることになると述べた。

Oct 21 : Toyota is recalling 105,794 vehicles in the US over a potential fuel leak that could raise the risk of fire if it reaches an ignition source, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said on Wednesday. Here are some details: • The recall involves certain 2024-2027 Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrid vehicles, the auto safety regulator said • The recall is over issues with the fuel tube connection near the fuel tank, which could disconnect and leak fuel, and increase the risk of a fire, the regulator said • As part of the remedy, dealers will install a supplemental clamp or replace the resin fuel tube free of charge, NHTSA said
